Honeybees do far more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower collecting nectar, they carry pollen along with them. This pollen helps plants make seeds and fruit. In fact, about one out of every three bites of food people eat depends on bees and other insects that move pollen between plants. Without honeybees, many of the fruits and vegetables we count on would become scarce. Honeybees are tiny, but they play a vital role in growing the food people eat.

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

A) Honeybees play a vital role in growing the food that people eat.
B) Honeybees
C) Honeybees move from flower to flower collecting nectar.
D) Honeybees are too small to matter very much.
items.answer: A) Honeybees play a vital role in growing the food that people eat.

steps: The central idea is the main point the author develops across the whole passage. Every detail (carrying pollen, one in three bites of food, fruits becoming scarce) builds toward the idea that honeybees are essential to growing food.
B) 'Honeybees' is only the topic, a one-word subject, not a complete statement of the main point.
C) Moving from flower to flower is a single supporting detail, not the overall point.
D) The passage says honeybees play a vital role, so the claim that they do not matter contradicts the text.

Recycling at home is easier than many people think. Sorting paper, plastic, and glass into separate bins takes only a few minutes a day. Those sorted materials are then turned into new products instead of being buried in a landfill. Studies show that a single household that recycles carefully can keep hundreds of pounds of trash out of landfills each year. Small daily choices, added up, make a real difference. Recycling at home can meaningfully reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills.

Which choice states a central idea of the passage rather than just the topic?

A) Recycling
B) Bins
C) Recycling at home can meaningfully reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills.
D) Trash
items.answer: C) Recycling at home can meaningfully reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills.

steps: A central idea is a complete statement of the main point the author develops, not a one-word subject. Choice C states the main point the passage builds toward.
A) 'Recycling' is the topic, a single word, not a central idea.
B) 'Bins' names a detail, not the main point.
D) 'Trash' is just a topic word, not a statement about it.

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Oak trees survive by producing far more seeds than can ever grow into new trees. A single oak tree can drop ten thousand acorns in a single year. Squirrels, deer, and birds eat most of these acorns. Many others land in shade or dry soil where they cannot sprout. Yet because the tree makes so many, a few acorns always reach good ground and grow. This is how oaks keep their forests alive year after year.

The central idea is that oak trees survive by producing far more seeds than can ever grow. Which detail from the passage best develops this central idea?

A) Squirrels, deer, and birds eat acorns.
B) A single oak tree can drop ten thousand acorns in a single year.
C) Oak trees grow in forests.
D) Acorns can land in the shade.
items.answer: B) A single oak tree can drop ten thousand acorns in a single year.

steps: The central idea is about producing far more seeds than can grow. The fact that one tree drops ten thousand acorns directly shows that huge number of seeds.
A) That animals eat acorns is a detail, but it does not show how many seeds the tree makes.
C) That oaks grow in forests is general background, not evidence of overproducing seeds.
D) Acorns landing in shade explains why some fail, not how many the tree produces.

Many people picture deserts as empty, lifeless places, but they are full of clever survivors. The kangaroo rat never needs to drink water; it gets all the moisture it needs from the seeds it eats. Cactus plants store water in thick stems and protect it with sharp spines. Some desert animals sleep underground during the blazing day and hunt only at night, when the air is cool. The fennec fox has huge ears that release heat to keep its body from overheating. Across the desert, living things have developed surprising features that let them thrive where water is scarce and the sun is harsh.

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?

A) The kangaroo rat never needs to drink water.
B) Desert plants and animals have developed special features that help them survive where water is scarce and the heat is harsh.
C) Deserts
D) Deserts are empty, lifeless places.
items.answer: B) Desert plants and animals have developed special features that help them survive where water is scarce and the heat is harsh.

steps: The central idea must cover the whole passage. Each example (kangaroo rat, cactus, night hunters, fennec fox) is a special survival feature, so the main point is that desert life has adaptations for harsh conditions.
A) The kangaroo rat is one example, a single detail, too narrow to be the central idea.
C) 'Deserts' is only the topic, not a complete statement of the point.
D) The passage opens by correcting this idea, then shows deserts are full of life, so it contradicts the text.

For most of history, people had no fast way to send news over long distances. A letter might take weeks to travel by ship or horse. Then, in the 1840s, the telegraph changed everything. By sending electric signals through wires, it could carry a message across a country in minutes instead of weeks. Newspapers used it to print stories the same day events happened. Businesses used it to send orders and prices quickly. Families used it to share urgent news. The telegraph did not just speed up messages; it connected distant places in a way the world had never seen before.

Which choice is the best objective summary of the passage?

A) The telegraph, invented in the 1840s, used electric signals to carry messages across great distances in minutes, and people used it for news, business, and personal messages, connecting distant places far faster than before.
B) The telegraph was the most amazing invention ever made, and everyone should be grateful for it.
C) Before the telegraph, a letter might take weeks to travel by ship or horse.
D) The telegraph used electric signals sent through wires.
items.answer: A) The telegraph, invented in the 1840s, used electric signals to carry messages across great distances in minutes, and people used it for news, business, and personal messages, connecting distant places far faster than before.

steps: An objective summary states the central idea and key supporting points without opinion. Choice A names the central idea (the telegraph connected distant places quickly) and the main supporting points (how it worked, who used it).
B) 'Most amazing invention ever' and 'everyone should be grateful' are personal opinions, not objective.
C) This is one detail from the opening, not a summary of the whole passage.
D) This gives only how the telegraph worked and leaves out the central idea and other key points.

Passage: Sea turtles face many dangers on their journey to survive. After hatching on a beach, baby turtles must rush to the ocean while birds and crabs try to eat them. In the water, they face hungry fish and pollution such as plastic bags, which they sometimes mistake for jellyfish. Only about one in a thousand sea turtles lives to become an adult. Scientists and volunteers now protect nesting beaches and clean up trash to give the turtles a better chance.

Draft summary: Sea turtles face many dangers, from predators on the beach to pollution in the ocean, and only about one in a thousand survives to adulthood. People are working to protect them, which proves we must all do more right now.

Which part of the draft summary is a personal opinion rather than an objective statement of what the text says?

A) Sea turtles face many dangers, from predators on the beach to pollution in the ocean.
B) Only about one in a thousand survives to adulthood.
C) Which proves we must all do more right now.
D) People are working to protect them.
items.answer: C) Which proves we must all do more right now.

steps: An objective summary reports what the text says without adding the writer's reactions or calls to action. 'We must all do more right now' is the writer's judgment, not information from the passage.
A) This objectively restates the dangers the passage describes.
B) The one-in-a-thousand statistic comes directly from the text.
D) The passage states that scientists and volunteers protect beaches and clean up trash, so this is objective.

For a long time, people believed that the brain stopped changing once a person grew up. Scientists thought you were born with all the brain cells and connections you would ever have. New research has overturned that idea. Studies now show that the brain keeps reshaping itself throughout life through a process called neuroplasticity. When you practice a skill, such as playing the piano or learning a language, the connections between brain cells grow stronger. When a skill goes unused, those connections weaken. Researchers have even watched the brains of adults form new pathways after an injury, finding fresh routes around damaged areas. This does not mean change is instant or easy; building strong connections takes steady practice over time. But the evidence is clear. Far from being fixed, the adult brain is flexible, and the things a person does and practices can physically shape how the brain is wired.

Which statement most fully captures the central idea of the passage?

A) The adult brain is not fixed; through neuroplasticity, a person's practice and experiences can physically reshape how the brain is wired throughout life.
B) When you practice playing the piano, the connections between brain cells grow stronger.
C) Scientists once believed the brain stopped changing once a person grew up.
D) The brain can form new pathways after an injury.
items.answer: A) The adult brain is not fixed; through neuroplasticity, a person's practice and experiences can physically reshape how the brain is wired throughout life.

steps: The passage builds from an old belief to new evidence, and every example (practice strengthening connections, unused skills weakening, recovery after injury) supports the broad point that the brain stays changeable. Choice A captures that full point.
B) The piano example develops the idea but covers only one section, so it is too narrow.
C) This is the outdated belief the passage corrects, not its central idea.
D) Forming new pathways after injury is one supporting detail, not the whole main point.

Light pollution is a problem most people never notice. In and around cities, streetlights, signs, and buildings send so much light into the night sky that the stars almost disappear. This wasted glow does more than hide the stars. It confuses migrating birds, which navigate by natural light and can crash into bright buildings. It disrupts the hunting and resting patterns of nocturnal animals. It even affects people, because bright nights can interfere with the sleep our bodies expect in darkness. The good news is that light pollution is one of the easiest kinds of pollution to fix. Shielding lights so they point downward, using softer bulbs, and turning off unneeded lights can bring back the dark night, often while saving energy too.

Which choice is the best objective summary of the passage?

A) Light pollution from artificial lighting harms wildlife and people and hides the stars, but it is one of the easiest kinds of pollution to fix with simple changes like shielding and dimming lights.
B) Light pollution hides the stars, and it is shameful that cities let this happen when the solution is so obvious.
C) Streetlights, signs, and buildings send light into the night sky so that the stars almost disappear in cities.
D) Light pollution harms migrating birds, nocturnal animals, and human sleep, and scientists are not sure whether it can ever be fixed.
items.answer: A) Light pollution from artificial lighting harms wildlife and people and hides the stars, but it is one of the easiest kinds of pollution to fix with simple changes like shielding and dimming lights.

steps: A complete, objective summary states the central idea and key points in order without opinion. Choice A covers both halves of the passage: the harms of light pollution and the fact that it is easy to fix.
B) 'It is shameful' inserts a personal judgment, so it is not objective.
C) This restates only one detail from the opening and leaves out the harms and the solution.
D) This adds information the passage never states; the text says light pollution is easy to fix, not that scientists doubt it can be fixed.
